nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and write $T(x) = \mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$ for its combined tail at a real number $x$. Then $T$ is antitone: $T(b) \le T(a)$ whenever $a \le b$.
nodes.title: The combined tail is antitone

nodes.summary: For every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every real number $x$, the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ satisfies $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x)) \le 2$.
nodes.title: The combined tail of a probability measure is at most two

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a real number $x$, the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$, where each of the two measures is converted from $[0, \infty]$ to a real number, an infinite value becoming $0$.
nodes.title: Combined tail of a measure

nodes.summary: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$ and $c > 0$, then $x \mapsto c f(x)$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$.
nodes.title: Positive multiples of regularly varying functions

nodes.summary: If $L : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is slowly varying and $c > 0$, then $x \mapsto c L(x)$ is slowly varying.
nodes.title: Positive multiples of slowly varying functions

nodes.summary: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with some index $\rho$, then $f(x) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$.
nodes.title: Regularly varying functions are eventually positive

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$. If $\mu((x, \infty)) = 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$ and the combined tail $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$ is positive for all sufficiently large $x$, then $\mu$ has tail balance $0$.
nodes.title: Tail balance zero from a vanishing right tail

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $p$ a real number. Write $R(x) = \mu((x, \infty))$ for the right tail and $T(x) = \mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$ for the combined tail of $\mu$. The measure $\mu$ has tail balance $p$ when $0 \le p \le 1$, $T(x) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$, and $R(x) / T(x) \to p$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Tail balance

nodes.summary: For real numbers $c > 0$ and $\rho$, the function $x \mapsto c x^\rho$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$.
nodes.title: Positive multiples of powers are regularly varying

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$, the function $x \mapsto x^\rho$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$.
nodes.title: Powers are regularly varying

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\rho \in \mathbb{R}$ if there is a slowly varying function $L : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x) = x^{\rho} L(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$.
nodes.title: Regularly varying function

nodes.summary: For every real $c > 0$, the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is slowly varying.
nodes.title: Positive constants are slowly varying

nodes.summary: The function $x \mapsto 1 + (1 + x)^{-1}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is slowly varying; it tends to the positive limit $1$ at infinity.
nodes.title: The function $1 + (1 + x)^{-1}$ is slowly varying

nodes.summary: The constant function $x \mapsto 1$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is slowly varying.
nodes.title: The constant function one is slowly varying

nodes.summary: A function $L : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is slowly varying (at infinity) if $L(x) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$ and, for every real $c > 0$, $L(cx) / L(x) \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Slowly varying function

nodes.summary: Karamata's integral theorem for antitone functions with a ratio limit. If `W` is antitone, nonnegative, bounded, eventually positive and `W (c * x) / W x → c ^ ρ` for every `c > 0`, then for `β ≥ 0` and `β + 1 + ρ > 0`, `(∫ t in (0)..x, t ^ β * W t) / (x ^ (β + 1) * W x) → 1 / (β + 1 + ρ)`. The proof substitutes `t = x * u` and applies dominated convergence with Potter's bound as the dominator.
nodes.title: Karamata's integral theorem

nodes.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the left tail of $\mu$ is antitone in the threshold: if $a \le b$, then $\mu((-\infty, -b)) \le \mu((-\infty, -a))$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the left tail

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every real $x$, the left tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$.
nodes.title: The left tail is at most the combined tail

nodes.summary: For every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every real $x$, the left tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The left tail of a probability measure is at most one

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a real $x$, the left tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((-\infty, -x))$, where an infinite value is sent to $0$.
nodes.title: Left tail of a measure

nodes.summary: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$ and $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is regularly varying with index $\sigma$, then the pointwise product $fg$ is regularly varying with index $\rho + \sigma$.
nodes.title: Products of regularly varying functions

nodes.summary: If $L_1, L_2 : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ are slowly varying, then so is their pointwise product $x \mapsto L_1(x) L_2(x)$.
nodes.title: Products of slowly varying functions

nodes.summary: For every $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and every $p \in \mathbb{R}$, the Dirac measure $\delta_a$ at $a$ does not have tail balance $p$.
nodes.title: Dirac masses have no tail balance

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and let $p \in \mathbb{R}$. If the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ equals $0$ for all sufficiently large $x$, then $\mu$ does not have tail balance $p$.
nodes.title: Eventually vanishing combined tail rules out tail balance

nodes.summary: Let $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\rho \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$ and $f(x) = g(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$, then $g$ is regularly varying with index $\rho$.
nodes.title: Regular variation is preserved by eventual equality

nodes.summary: Let $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. If $f$ is slowly varying and $f(x) = g(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$, then $g$ is slowly varying.
nodes.title: Slow variation is preserved by eventual equality

nodes.summary: Let $L : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a > 0$. If $L(x) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$ and $L(x) \to a$ as $x \to \infty$, then $L$ is slowly varying.
nodes.title: Functions with a positive limit are slowly varying

nodes.summary: Potter's bound for antitone functions with a ratio limit. If `W` is antitone, bounded, eventually positive and `W (c * x) / W x → c ^ ρ` for every `c > 0`, then for every `δ > 0` there are `C > 0` and `Y` such that `W (x * u) / W x ≤ C * u ^ (ρ - δ)` for all `x ≥ Y` and `u ∈ (0, 1]`. The proof chains the ratio limit at the dyadic scales `1/2` and `2`.
nodes.title: Potter's bound

nodes.summary: A regularly varying function has the expected ratio limit.
nodes.title: Ratio limit of a regularly varying function

nodes.summary: For a regularly varying function `f` of index `-α` with `α > 0` that is eventually non-increasing, there exists a sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` of positive reals such that `n · f (a n) → 1` as `n → ∞`.
nodes.title: Generalized inverse of a regularly varying function

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$. If $x \le y$, then the right tail of $\mu$ at $y$ is at most the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$.
nodes.title: The right tail of a finite measure is antitone

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$.
nodes.title: The right tail is at most the combined tail

nodes.summary: For every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The right tail of a probability measure is at most one

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((x, \infty))$ when $\mu((x, \infty)) < \infty$, and $0$ when $\mu((x, \infty)) = \infty$.
nodes.title: Right tail of a measure

nodes.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the combined tail $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$, with both masses taken as real numbers, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The combined tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity

nodes.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the left tail $\mu((-\infty, -x))$, taken as a real number, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The left tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity

nodes.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the right tail $\mu((x, \infty))$, taken as a real number, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The right tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
